author: VINCENT LUCARELLI
title: Leaders hail sale of Shops at Fallen Timbers as catalyst for growth - NewsBreak
text:
By VINCENT LUCARELLI ,
6 hours ago
The Shops at Fallen Timbers were sold on Tuesday, officials said.
The buyer was a consortium called Timbers Town Center Ltd., which is composed of several developers with ties to Columbus and that city’s Easton Town Center development.
“The cost for the redevelopment planned for Timbers Town Center — including the acquisition cost — will be approximately $89 million,” said Tim Rollins, a developer who is part of the consortium.
Mr. Rollins did not disclose an exact acquisition cost. The Lucas County Auditor’s Office said Wednesday that public records related to the sale were not yet available because it takes a couple of days for sales of this kind to process into its real estate database.
Brian McMahon, owner and president of Danberry National commercial realty firm, said the revitalization of the Fallen Timbers area puts Maumee at the axis of a major corridor of activity.
“This is a very significant event that is going to trigger a lot more development in that area,” said Mr. McMahon, who has long had interests in the area the mall sits on.
He connects the Fallen Timbers area with the development at Waterville Landing to the west, where a Meijer is being constructed, and ongoing work at the former St. Luke’s Hospital property to the east.
“This is more than just the sale of the shopping center,” Mr. McMahon said. “I think that this is probably the most dynamic, exciting thing that’s going to happen in the city of Maumee in a long time. They have never had that number of projects that are within their city and it won’t just be the real estate tax, it will be a lot of income tax.”
Maumee Mayor Chelsea Ziss is also excited about the prospect of what the redeveloped mall could be.
“I know that it was a long road to get there, and I am very glad it closed,” said the mayor, who noted the city and the developers have been in contact for at least the last nine months.
She said the city is bound to have an explosion of economic development and community development as these projects get off the ground.
“That they’re committed to not just doing something to make money but to leave a legacy and make a mark and have it expand and grow is just incredible,” Ms. Ziss said of the developers.
She added that the mall’s developers want to tackle things right away. Their priorities are to work on maintaining what is already on the property and making the mall as a whole more accessible. This is in addition to making sure storefronts are filled.
“It will be one of the premier shopping malls and mixed-use centers in the area again, just like it once was,” Ms. Ziss said. “It will only be better.”
